newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp says owns no Thyssen shares.
newsitem.headline: Krupp says owns no Thyssen shares.

text.p: German industrial group Krupp on Friday denied a newspaper report it had secured control of a 30 percent stake in Thyssen AG, with which it has started merger talks after suspending a hostile takeover bid.

Commenting on the report in the Handelsblatt daily, a Krupp spokesman said: "That is not correct. We do not have any Thyssen shares." The spokesman added that Krupp's banks had not bought any Thyssen shares on its behalf.
The denial repeats earlier comments by Fried. Krupp AG Krupp-Hoesch that it did not hold any Thyssen shares.

Krupp had launched a hostile takeover bid valuing Thyssen at a 25 percent premium to its share capitalisation, but the two sides on Thursday began eight days of talks to try and find a way to cooperate on a friendly basis.
Sources close to the negotiations said earlier that the Handelsblatt report was highly speculative, but added Krupp may have taken steps to make sure it can get hold of Thyssen stock.

"Whether it is 10 percent or 30 percent, that I cannot say," the source said. "But the whole reason this came up in the first place is that Thyssen had no protection for its shares. It (Thyssen) didn't even know who its shareholders were. So naturally Krupp will have taken some steps."
Handelsblatt said that Krupp was still interested in taking control of its rival and had also secured a 15 billion mark line of credit from banks.
But None of Krupp's Frankfurt-based banks -- Dresdner Bank AG, Deutsche Bank AG or Goldman Sachs -- was prepared to comment on details of the report.
